title: Open-Source Project Ditches AI Ban for a 'Slop Reduction Policy'!
summary: Open-source firmware project Libreboot deleted its month-old AGENTS.md ban on AI-generated contributions on November 20 after maintainer Leah Rowe deemed it unenforceable. The project replaced the blanket prohibition with a practical 'Slop Reduction Policy' focused on submission quality.
raw_text: So check this out—one of the most relatable open-source policy reversals just happened! Open-source firmware project Libreboot deleted its month-old AGENTS.md ban on AI contributions after maintainer Leah Rowe admitted an outright ban is basically unenforceable, replacing it with a 'Slop Reduction Policy' instead. Here's the wild part: trying to police whether a contributor used an AI assistant under the hood is nearly impossible when upstream code already has AI touches and detection tools aren't reliable. Honestly, this is huge for open-source maintainers everywhere because focusing on code quality and filtering out low-effort AI slop makes way more practical sense than unenforceable blanket bans.
